coverageDimensions:
REGION coverage would mean: in which AWS Regions does this capability operate. This page gives you the negative half of it, and only per control. It names 38 Regions, each with a list of controls that do not work there. It does not state the set of Regions where Security Hub CSPM runs, so it supplies no denominator. A Region not on this page is ambiguous: fully covered, or not offered at all. To turn this page into region coverage you must join it to two things it does not contain - the AWS Region universe, and the Security Hub CSPM supported-Region list from elsewhere. What the page does give, and gives well, is 6,313 exact negative facts to subtract once you have those.

SERVICE coverage would mean: which AWS services Security Hub CSPM has controls for. This page gives you nothing. The 80 service prefixes visible in the control IDs are, by construction, only services with at least one regional gap. A service whose controls all work in every Region appears nowhere on this page. Reading a service list off these prefixes produces a list that is both incomplete and inverted in meaning.

RESOURCE TYPE coverage would mean: which AWS resource types the controls evaluate. This page gives you nothing at all, and there is no partial signal to salvage. Resource types appear only as English inside control titles ("ElastiCache replication groups", "SageMaker notebook instances", "S3 directory buckets"). They are never enumerated, never normalised to a resource type identifier, and never the subject of a claim. Parsing resource types out of control titles here would be fabrication, not extraction.

Summary: this page is one dimension deep. It is a per-control regional exclusion list and nothing else. It is a subtrahend, not a coverage source - useful only in combination with the control catalogue and the supported-Region list, both of which live on other pages.

features.featureName: Regional limits on Security Hub CSPM controls
features.reasoning: There is exactly one capability here: a Security Hub CSPM control. The claim shape on the page is "control X does not reach Region Y", so the value set being enumerated against is the AWS Region, and the control is the thing whose reach is described. Region is the correct axis because it is EXTERNAL: AWS Regions exist independently of Security Hub, so "38 of N Regions" is a meaningful denominator once N comes from the Region universe. The control dimension is deliberately NOT the axis, because the set of Security Hub CSPM controls is a CATALOGUE that Security Hub publishes about itself. Security Hub holds 100% of its own control catalogue by definition, so a figure like "522 controls" or "522 of 522" is not coverage and must never be shown as a ratio. Declaring one feature rather than two is correct: a second entry on the control axis would be the same capability counted twice, and it would be the catalogue-ratio mistake. Note also that expectedCount 38 is the number of Regions the page NAMES, which is not the number of Regions Security Hub CSPM supports. The page enumerates only Regions that have at least one exclusion. A Region absent from this page is unresolvable from this page alone: it is either fully covered or a Region where Security Hub CSPM is not offered at all. The page never states which.
features.scope: Per control. The page is a control x Region matrix expressed as 38 Region sections; 522 distinct control IDs appear, producing 6,313 (control, Region) not-supported pairs.
features.statuses: 0 stated as covered, 6,313 stated as NOT covered. Every single bullet on the page is an exclusion: all 38 sections are introduced by the same sentence, "The following controls are not supported in the <Region> Region." There is no Yes/No column, no footnote, no retired or deprecated marking, and no positive statement anywhere. The one occurrence of the word "deprecated" on the page is inside a control title (CloudFront.10, "...should not use deprecated SSL protocols...") and is not a status marker. Per-Region exclusion counts, counted off the page: US East (N. Virginia) 6, US East (Ohio) 44, US West (N. California) 74, US West (Oregon) 27, Africa (Cape Town) 108, Asia Pacific (Hong Kong) 81, Asia Pacific (Hyderabad) 220, Asia Pacific (Jakarta) 160, Asia Pacific (Malaysia) 389, Asia Pacific (Melbourne) 233, Asia Pacific (Mumbai) 43, Asia Pacific (New Zealand) 436, Asia Pacific (Osaka) 114, Asia Pacific (Seoul) 57, Asia Pacific (Singapore) 35, Asia Pacific (Sydney) 32, Asia Pacific (Taipei) 511, Asia Pacific (Thailand) 411, Asia Pacific (Tokyo) 33, Canada (Central) 56, Canada West (Calgary) 375, China (Beijing) 250, China (Ningxia) 233, Europe (Frankfurt) 33, Europe (Ireland) 29, Europe (London) 53, Europe (Milan) 112, Europe (Paris) 61, Europe (Spain) 216, Europe (Stockholm) 69, Europe (Zurich) 211, Israel (Tel Aviv) 253, Mexico (Central) 418, Middle East (Bahrain) 115, Middle East (UAE) 201, South America (Sao Paulo) 64, AWS GovCloud (US-East) 280, AWS GovCloud (US-West) 270. pageTitle: Regional limits on Security Hub CSPM controls
shouldNotExtract: The **Topics** block of 38 anchor links immediately under the intro. It is navigation and it mirrors the 38 H2 headings exactly, so a parser that takes both the Topics bullets and the section headings double counts every Region. Take the H2 headings, not the Topics list. Also exclude: the H1 and the two intro paragraphs, including the console/aggregation-Region behaviour sentence ("a control doesn't appear in the list of controls if it isn't available in the Region that you're currently signed in to... The exception is an aggregation Region") - that is console display behaviour, not a coverage claim. Exclude the entire "See also" H2 and its single bullet about "Skills for AI coding assistants (optional)" and the `aws agent-toolkit search-skills` command - that is AWS boilerplate now appended to every page and contains no coverage. Exclude the `<a name="...">` anchor tags. Exclude the link targets on every bullet (elasticache-controls.md#elasticache-4, s3-controls.md#s3-24, and so on) - they are cross-page references, not values. There are no quotas, prices, prerequisites, code examples, or troubleshooting on this page.
trap: Sign inversion. The page reads like a big supported-controls list and is in fact the exact opposite: every one of the 6,313 bullets is an exclusion. A parser that scrapes the bullets and records them as supported produces 6,313 claims that are each precisely backwards - the worst possible failure, since it would assert coverage exactly where AWS says there is none. The single-word cue is in the repeated section sentence: "are not supported". A second trap is treating this page as an inventory: it is a delta, not a catalogue. The 522 control IDs here are only the controls that are unavailable somewhere, and the 38 Regions are only the Regions with at least one gap - neither is the full universe, and neither denominator lives on this page. A third trap is deriving a service list from the control ID prefixes: 80 distinct prefixes (ACM, APIGateway, ... WorkSpaces) appear, but they are the services that have a gap somewhere, so building service coverage from them inverts the meaning again. Note the prefixes are not even clean - both "AutoScaling" and "Autoscaling" appear as written, so naive prefix grouping splits one service in two. A fourth trap is reading "deprecated" inside the CloudFront.10 title as a control status.
whatThePageStates: The page is a pure exclusion list: it names, Region by Region, the Security Hub CSPM controls that are NOT available there. It has 38 Region sections, each opening with the identical sentence "The following controls are not supported in the <Region> Region." followed by a bullet list of control IDs and titles. Across the 38 sections there are 6,313 bullets, drawn from 522 distinct control IDs. The only other content is one paragraph explaining that an unavailable control is hidden from the console except in an aggregation Region, a Topics block of 38 anchor links, and a "See also" block.
